name: tma_multicast
kind: service-axis measurement: does a multicast TMA tile load use the SM delivery path and the shared read path once per destination CTA; no workload-based fitting
question: A UTMALDG .MULTICAST load of a 2-CTA cluster is read once and delivered to both CTAs. When every SM of the card runs such loads, is the sustainable box rate that of plain loads counted per issued box (the read side limits) or per delivered box (the delivery side limits: half the issue rate when every CTA both issues and receives)? And on one cluster without card load, does a received box occupy the receiving SM's delivery port?
motivation: Hardware counters of full-gpu cases with multicast loads show l1tex__m_xbar2l1tex_read_sectors x 32 B equal to the box bytes times the number of destination CTAs (cublas_fp16_big_square_01: 201 MB delivered for 134 MB of boxes, two thirds of the instances multicast; flashinfer_segment_01: 100.8 MB for 50.3 MB, all multicast) while L2 read sectors count the box once. In flashinfer_segment_00 / 01 / 02 the consumers wait for TMA data ~900 cycles per k iteration on hardware (about 50 in the engine); each SM there receives about 24 KiB per 1000 cycles, 85 % of the full-card rate the tma_loaded / tma_oob probes measured for plain loads (28.8 KiB per 1000 cycles and SM at 132 SMs), but only 43 % if a multicast box is counted once ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/fg-over20/notes/NOTES.md, lead B'). The engine charges a multicast load like a plain load of the issuing SM: the memory path has no destination count.
probe: tma_multicast.cu from tools/microbench/tma_loaded/probe/tma_loaded.cu (same 64 x 128 bf16 SWIZZLE_128B box of 16 KiB, hot 24-MiB tensor resident in L2 after the discarded first launch, one warp per slot: expect_tx, load, test_wait spin, re-issue; global arrival counter; per-CTA bytes, clock window, latency samples). Launch with cluster dimension 2 along x (cudaLaunchKernelEx / __cluster_dims__(2, 1, 1)), one CTA per SM. Modes: plain = the non-multicast instruction, every CTA loads for itself (control: must reproduce tma_loaded); mc_both = every CTA issues .multicast::cluster loads with mask 0b11 into slot s of both CTAs (each CTA owns half of the slot range as issuer: CTA rank r issues slots s with s % 2 == r, both CTAs' mbarriers of that slot expect the box, the issuer's warp waits on its own); mc_one = only rank-0 CTAs issue (all their slots, mask 0b11), rank-1 CTAs only receive (their warps wait on their own mbarriers and count bytes). Cells: N in {2, 16, all SMs (even count)} x S in {2, 4, 8} x mode; 2048 rounds, 8 samples, runs a and b. Rates are reported per issuing CTA (boxes issued per 1000 cycles) and per SM as delivered boxes (issued + received). Counter pass (ncu, cache-control none) for N = all, S = 4 of each mode: lts__t_sectors_srcunit_tex_op_read.sum, l1tex__m_xbar2l1tex_read_sectors.sum, dram__bytes_read.sum, sm__cycles_active.max.

controls.sass: plain kernel: UTMALDG.2D without .MULTICAST; multicast kernels: UTMALDG.2D.MULTICAST; counts per kernel recorded.
controls.data: after the last round a receiving CTA checks the first 64 B of a slot it did not issue (memset pattern); a wrong sum fails the cell.
controls.timing: plain cells reproduce tma_loaded / tma_oob x = 0 of the same device within 10 % (rate and latency p50) at N = all and N = 2 (against N = 1); runs a and b within 10 %.
controls.counters: xbar read sectors per issued box = 512 (plain), 1024 (multicast); L2 tex read sectors per issued box about 512 in all modes.

derivation: issue_rate(mode, N, S) = boxes issued per 1000 cycles per issuing CTA; delivered_rate = boxes delivered per 1000 cycles per SM (plain: = issue rate; mc_both: = 2 x issue rate x 1/2 + ... = issue rate of the SM + boxes received = 2 x per-CTA issue rate when both issue equally; mc_one: rank 0 and rank 1 SMs each receive what rank 0 issues). Ratios against plain at the same N and S.

predictions_before_data.engine_today: issue rate of mc_both = plain at every N and S (a multicast box costs what a plain box costs, on the issuing SM only); mc_one: rank-0 issue rate = plain.
predictions_before_data.delivery_limited: N = all: delivered boxes per SM are capped at the plain rate (about 1.8 per 1000 cycles on h100 at S >= 4) -> mc_both issue rate per CTA = plain / 2 x (per SM delivered = plain), mc_one rank-0 issue rate = plain (each SM receives one box per issued box). N = 2, S = 8 (per-SM delivery port, 6.4 boxes per 1000 cycles plain on h100): mc_both delivered per SM capped at 6.4 -> issue rate per CTA 3.2 with S / 2 = 4 own slots (plain with 4 slots: 5.4) - visible only if the port binds.
predictions_before_data.read_limited: N = all: mc_both issue rate per CTA = plain x (S / 2 slots effect only); delivered per SM up to twice the plain rate.

outcomes_before_data.delivery: If at N = all the delivered rate per SM of mc_both is within 15 % of the plain rate (and the issue rate about half): rule = every sector of a multicast tile load passes the receiving SM's delivery port and the shared (per-GPC / device) read services once per destination CTA; the engine needs the destination CTAs of the load (cluster rank mask, a capture fact already in the trace as the multicast mask) and charges the non-issuing destinations like phantom sectors on their SMs. No new leaf value.
outcomes_before_data.read: If the issue rate of mc_both at N = all is within 15 % of plain at the same number of own slots: the engine's present accounting stands; the segment deficit is elsewhere.
outcomes_before_data.between: Otherwise: report rates and counters; addendum with the form (for example delivery counted with a weight) before any install.

prediction_check: H100 replay is limited to one cluster (N = 2): mc_both and plain at S = 8 within 15 %; the N = all behaviour is checked by the full-gpu 500 x 2 regression against main's baseline (fg-over20/full-h1) and the per-role waits of the named cases.
not_allowed: No family / case / shape specific timing; no tuning to the full-gpu error; post-data changes of a criterion are labelled with their reason.

addenda.runs: $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/tma_multicast/{h100-r2,b300-r2} (36 + 36 rows each, no error rows; r1 are failed rounds; a handshake-free control plain_nohs was added to the cells before the run that counts)
addenda.text: Boxes per 1000 cycles, S = 8. plain_nohs (= tma_loaded): h100 6.44 / 3.70 / 1.80 at N = 2 / 16 / 132, b300 7.60 / 7.56 / 4.15 at N = 2 / 16 / 148 - the control reproduces tma_loaded. The handshake variant of plain is bound by the handshake itself (0.37-1.31 at every N) and is not a usable reference; the comparison below is against plain_nohs, which changes the declared control (stated as such). mc_both, N = all: h100 1.37 issued per CTA = 2.74 delivered per SM; b300 1.71 issued = 3.41 delivered. mc_one, N = all: h100 2.61 issued by rank 0 and delivered to every SM; b300 6.24. Counters: xbar read sectors = 2 x L2 tex read sectors in both multicast modes, equal in plain. Outcome: 'read' in substance - delivered boxes per SM exceed the plain full-card cap (h100 2.74 and 2.61 against 1.80), so the full-card limit is not on delivery and a multicast box does not cost the shared path once per destination; prediction delivery_limited is rejected, the engine's accounting (a multicast load is charged once, on the read side) stands, nothing installed. The starvation of the flashinfer_segment consumers is not explained by multicast delivery. Not explained and not modelled: multicast rates fall with N while still below the read cap (h100 mc_one S = 8: 4.24 / 3.85 / 2.61 at N = 2 / 16 / 132 with latency 634 / 795 / 1372; at N = 132 the L2 read side carries 5.3 kB per ns of 7.6).
